newsitem.title: VATICAN: Vatican signs pact on Hungarian Catholic Church.
newsitem.headline: Vatican signs pact on Hungarian Catholic Church.

text.p: The Vatican signed a pact with Hungary on Friday covering settlement of claims over property seized under communism, financing of the Roman Catholic Church and protection of its social and educational activities.
Vatican Secretary of State Cardinal Angelo Sodano, who signed the pact with Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn, hailed it as the start of a new era in mutual relations.
"This may serve as an example to other countries which have emerged from communism to face similar problems of an economic nature," Sodano said at a signing ceremony at the Vatican.
The five-part pact, which has been criticised by Horn's coalition partners, the Free Democrats, gives Roman Catholic schools the same status as state institutions.
The Church, which counts nearly two thirds of Hungarians among its followers, will also be guaranteed adequate autonomous financing to sustain its religious activities.

The pact foresees that through the return of property seized under communism, state compensation for property which cannot be returned and the decision to allow Hungarians to direct 1.1 percent of their taxes to a chosen church or charity.
The Vatican denied the deal gave the Catholic Church privileged status over Hungary's non-Catholic believers, mostly Protestants and Jews.

The Free Democrats have criticised the agreement on the grounds that singling out one religion for support might be unconstitutional and could have a negative effect on the funding of other independent schools.
The pact now needs to be ratified by Hungary's parliament.
